questions.q: Match the eyelid muscle with its nerve supply — 1) Levator palpebrae superioris  2) Müller's muscle  3) Orbicularis oculi  … A) Sympathetic fibres  B) CN III  C) CN VII
questions.exp: 3 muscles table: Levator palpebrae superioris - CN III; Müller's muscle - sympathetic fibres; Orbicularis oculi - CN VII. (Book p206)

questions.q: Elevation of the upper lid is produced by the levator palpebrae superioris and ___.
questions.exp: Levator palpebrae superioris and Müller's muscle both elevate the upper lid; orbicularis oculi closes the eyelid. (Book p206)

questions.q: Palsy of the orbicularis oculi (CN VII) presents as ___.
questions.exp: Orbicularis oculi - CN VII - closure of eyelid; presentation in palsy: lagophthalmos. (Palsy of the lid elevators presents as ptosis.) (Book p206)

questions.q: Match the eyelid gland with its type — 1) Meibomian (tarsal) gland  2) Moll gland  … A) Modified sweat gland  B) Modified sebaceous gland
questions.exp: 3 glands: meibomian (tarsal) - modified sebaceous; Zeis - modified sebaceous; moll - modified sweat. (Book p206)

questions.q: The meibomian (tarsal) gland opens ___ to the anterior surface of the eyelid margin.
questions.exp: Meibomian (tarsal) gland: modified sebaceous, opens posterior to anterior surface of eyelid margin. (Book p206)

questions.q: Which gland of the eyelid is a modified sebaceous gland that opens at the base of the lash follicles?
questions.exp: Zeis - modified sebaceous - opens at base of lash follicles. (Moll gland opens there too but is a modified sweat gland.) (Book p206)

questions.q: The grey line divides the eyelid into the anterior lamina and the ___.
questions.exp: EYELID: Grey line divides eyelid into anterior lamina and posterior lamina (schematic label: Gray line). (Book p206)

questions.q: The anterior lamina of the eyelid consists of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Anterior lamina: skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscles. The tarsal plate and palpebral conjunctiva belong to the posterior lamina. (Book p206)

questions.q: The skin of the eyelid is:
opts: The thickest skin in the body
The thinnest skin in the body
questions.exp: Anterior lamina: skin - thinnest skin in the body. (Book p206)

questions.q: The tarsal plate of the posterior lamina contains only ___ tissue.
questions.exp: Posterior: tarsal plate has only fibrous tissue. (Book p206)

questions.q: The posterior lamina of the eyelid consists of the tarsal plate and:
questions.exp: Posterior lamina: tarsal plate (only fibrous tissue) and palpebral conjunctiva. (Book p206)

questions.q: In the schematic of the eyelid, the Zeis & moll glands are shown opening at the base of the ___, while the meibomian gland opens behind the grey line.
questions.exp: Schematic labels: Gray line, Zeis & moll glands, meibomian gland, eye lash. (Book p206)

questions.q: Match the condition with its pathology — 1) Chalazion  2) External hordeolum/stye  … A) Suppurative inflammation of Zeis gland  B) Lipogranulomatous inflammation of meibomian gland
questions.exp: CHALAZION & HORDEOLUM: chalazion - lipogranulomatous inflammation of meibomian gland (non-infective); external hordeolum/stye - suppurative inflammation of Zeis gland (infective). (Book p206)

questions.q: External hordeolum/stye is infective, most commonly due to ___.
questions.exp: Infectivity: chalazion non-infective; external hordeolum infective - S. aureus. (Book p206)

questions.q: A patient has a painless, circumscribed swelling away from the lid margin (photograph of the appearance row). The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Swelling: chalazion - painless, circumscribed swelling away from lid margin (appearance row photographs). (Book p207)

questions.q: A patient has a painful, diffuse swelling at the lid margin. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: External hordeolum/stye: painful, diffuse swelling at the lid margin. (Book p207)

questions.q: Match the treatment of chalazion with its detail — 1) Incision & curettage  2) Intralesional injection  … A) Triamcinolone  B) Horizontal incision on the posterior part of the eyelid (conjunctiva)
questions.exp: Rx of chalazion: incision & curettage - horizontal incision on posterior part of eyelid (conjunctiva); intralesional triamcinolone. (Book p207)

questions.q: Treatment of external hordeolum/stye is:
opts: Incision and curettage with intralesional triamcinolone
Hot compresses, with oral antibiotics if recurrent
questions.exp: Rx hordeolum: hot compresses; oral antibiotics if recurrent. (Book p207)

questions.q: A chalazion recurs repeatedly. Which complication does the table warn about?
questions.exp: Complications - chalazion: recurrence -> sebaceous cell carcinoma. (Hordeolum: no complication listed, appearance row gives its photograph.) (Book p207)

questions.q: Hordeolum internum is suppurative inflammation of the ___ gland.
questions.exp: Hordeolum internum: suppurative inflammation of meibomian gland. (Book p207)

questions.q: Trichiasis is ___ of the eyelashes.
questions.exp: TRICHIASIS: inward misdirection of eyelashes. (Book p207)

questions.q: Trichiasis causes ___ of the cornea.
questions.exp: Trichiasis causes corneal opacity. (Book p207)

questions.q: The clinical photograph of lashes touching the globe on this page is captioned:
questions.exp: Photograph caption: Trichiasis - inward misdirection of eyelashes. (Book p207)

questions.q: Which is the definitive treatment of trichiasis?
questions.exp: Treatment: epilation every 1-2 months; cryotherapy of lash base - definitive. (Book p207)

questions.q: Entropion is inward turning of the ___.
questions.exp: ENTROPION & ECTROPION table: entropion - inward turning of eyelid margin (photograph of entropion). (Book p207)

questions.q: Outward turning of the eyelid margin, most commonly caused by senility, is called:
questions.exp: Ectropion - outward turning of eyelid margin; m/c cause: senility. (Book p207)

questions.q: Match the type of entropion with its operation — 1) Spastic  2) Senile  3) Cicatricial  … A) Modified Burrows operation, wedge resection  B) Botulinum toxin injection  C) Modified Wheeler operation, Weiss operation
questions.exp: Rx of entropion: spastic -> botulinum toxin injection; senile -> modified wheeler operation, weiss operation; cicatricial -> modified burrows operation, wedge resection. (Book p207)

questions.q: Which operation is listed for ectropion?
questions.exp: Rx of ectropion: medial conjunctivoplasty; burvon smith operation. (The other options are operations for entropion.) (Book p207)

questions.q: Besides medial conjunctivoplasty, the other operation listed for ectropion (as written in the book) is:
questions.exp: Rx of ectropion: medial conjunctivoplasty; burvon smith operation (the operation is written this way in the book). (Book p207)

questions.q: Distichiasis is an extra ___ row of eye lashes.
questions.exp: DISTICHIASIS: extra posterior row of eye lashes (photograph: distichiasis). (Book p208)

questions.q: A patient has lost the lateral one-third of his eye lashes and eyebrow due to chronic rubbing of the eye. This is called:
questions.exp: MADAROSIS: loss of lateral 1/3rd of eye lashes & eyebrow d/t chronic rubbing of the eye (photograph: madarosis). (Book p208)

questions.q: Tylosis is thickening of the ___.
questions.exp: TYLOSIS: thickening of eyelid margin. (Book p208)

questions.q: Fusion of the eyelid margins of the upper and lower lid, occurring after trauma, is:
questions.exp: ANKYLOBLEPHARON: fusion of eyelid margin of upper & lower lid; post trauma. (Book p208)

questions.q: Congenital ptosis is due to defective development of the ___.
questions.exp: CONGENITAL PTOSIS: d/t defective development of levator palpebrae superioris (photograph: congenital ptosis). (Book p208)

questions.q: The two clinical features of congenital ptosis given in the book are absent upper lid crease and:
questions.exp: Clinical features: absent upper lid crease; lid lag on downgaze - failure of eyelid to go down on downward gaze. (Book p208)

questions.q: Lid lag on downgaze in congenital ptosis means:
opts: Failure of the eyelid to move up on upward gaze
Failure of the eyelid to close on blinking
Failure of the eyelid to go down on downward gaze
Downward displacement of the lid on upgaze
questions.exp: Lid lag on downgaze: failure of eyelid to go down on downward gaze. (Book p208)

questions.q: Match the ptosis with its treatment — 1) Moderate ptosis, fair LPS function  2) Severe ptosis, poor LPS function  … A) Frontalis sling SX  B) LPS resection
questions.exp: Treatment table: moderate ptosis with fair LPS function -> LPS resection; severe ptosis with poor LPS function -> frontalis sling SX. (Book p208)

questions.q: Marcus Gunn jaw winking syndrome is due to ___ nerve synkinesis.
questions.exp: Marcus Gunn jaw winking syndrome: d/t trigemino-oculomotor nerve synkinesis. (Book p208)

questions.q: In Marcus Gunn jaw winking syndrome, what happens on opening the jaw?
opts: The lid droops further, while a closed jaw shows retraction
The lid moves up, while a closed jaw shows ptosis
questions.exp: Closed jaw -> ptosis; open jaw -> lid moves up. (Book p208)

units.title: Muscles of the eyelid
units.guide: Levator palpebrae superioris (CN III) and Müller's muscle (sympathetic) elevate the upper lid - palsy gives ptosis; orbicularis oculi (CN VII) closes the eyelid - palsy gives lagophthalmos.

units.title: Glands of the eyelid
units.guide: Meibomian (tarsal) = modified sebaceous gland opening posterior to the anterior surface of the eyelid margin; Zeis = modified sebaceous and Moll = modified sweat gland, both opening at the base of the lash follicles.

units.title: Structure of the eyelid
units.guide: Grey line divides the eyelid into anterior lamina (skin - thinnest in the body, subcutaneous tissue, muscles) and posterior lamina (tarsal plate of only fibrous tissue, palpebral conjunctiva); schematic labels: gray line, Zeis & moll glands, meibomian gland, eye lash.

units.title: Chalazion and hordeolum
units.guide: Chalazion = non-infective lipogranulomatous inflammation of meibomian gland, painless swelling away from the lid margin, incision & curettage (horizontal, posterior) or intralesional triamcinolone, recurrence may lead to sebaceous cell carcinoma; external hordeolum/stye = infective suppurative inflammation of Zeis gland (S. aureus), painful diffuse swelling at the lid margin, hot compresses + oral antibiotics if recurrent; hordeolum internum = meibomian gland.

units.title: Trichiasis
units.guide: Inward misdirection of eyelashes causing corneal opacity; epilation every 1-2 months, with cryotherapy of the lash base as the definitive treatment.

units.title: Entropion and ectropion
units.guide: Entropion = inward turning of the eyelid margin (spastic - botulinum toxin; senile - modified Wheeler/Weiss operation; cicatricial - modified Burrows operation, wedge resection); ectropion = outward turning of the eyelid margin, most commonly due to senility, treated by medial conjunctivoplasty or burvon smith operation.

units.title: Distichiasis, madarosis, tylosis and ankyloblepharon
units.guide: Distichiasis = extra posterior row of lashes; madarosis = loss of lateral 1/3rd of lashes and eyebrow due to chronic rubbing; tylosis = thickening of the eyelid margin; ankyloblepharon = post-traumatic fusion of the upper and lower eyelid margins.

units.title: Congenital ptosis and Marcus Gunn jaw winking syndrome
units.guide: Congenital ptosis from defective development of levator palpebrae superioris; absent upper lid crease and lid lag on downgaze; moderate ptosis with fair LPS function - LPS resection, severe ptosis with poor LPS function - frontalis sling Sx; Marcus Gunn jaw winking = trigemino-oculomotor synkinesis (closed jaw - ptosis, open jaw - lid moves up).
